title: ID0417862 - DC/Si-D/FI - [acno33] - Charging suddenly stopping in DC2 (C1)
description:
Customer states that DC2 (right main unit outlet) is cutting out middle of charging.
Seems that it might be potentially QA13-14 getting stuck.

additional_info.subject: 0418822 - ID0417862 - DC/Si-D/FI - [acno33] - Charging suddenly stopping in DC2 (C1) CRM:00314000163
additional_info.body:
Good evening colleagues,
I am reaching out regarding child case
ID0418822
opened for charging interruption on DC2 on charger
acno33.
I had a look at the logs of the event reported, as well as I conducted a quick investigation on AWS to see the frequency of occurrence of the issue. These are my findings:
At 2025-04-09T09:36:09 DC2 is connected
At 2025-04-09T09:36:43 DC2 starts charging
At 2025-04-09T09:59:19. DC2 stops charging
Even if it seems that the OGCAuxFbk goes to off, from past experience I noticed that in those cases in which the TDK contactor really loses the FBK, we should see subsequently an “Abnormal” status on the FBK, as the charger commands again the contactor to be closed.
In this case, I believe that the OGCAuxFbk goes to off as a consequence of EcoG error 67 “ERR_EV_DROPPED, vehicle ended with unexpected pilot state B”. I have seen this behavior before. The EVMAC of the vehicle was “00.7d.fa.09.62.a52”.
To confirm this analysis, we see subsequently a EcoG Error 35 “pilot stateC while stop charging”, as a sign that the CP signal from the EV had a drop.
I saw the same behavior on outlet DC2 on 2025-04-17, when DC2 started charging at 2025-04-17T10:18:18, then at 2025-04-17T10:44:15 the DC2 OGCAuxFbk goes to off, we see error code 67 and the charging stops. Also in this case, afterwards it comes a EcoG Error 35. The EVMAC in this case is
“
00.7d.fa.07.09.5d” (MEB Platform).
In conclusion, in my eyes I do not see a failure of QA13-14, but rather an incorrect behavior of the CP caused by the EV.
I attach the logs to this email for your reference.
Should you have further questions, please reply to this email.
